Maitland Corporation
Professional Development Fund
Information for All Full-Time Employees
About the Fund
The Professional Development Fund was established to promote ongoing professional growth throughout the organization. Beginning this quarter, the fund has been expanded to include all full-time employees who have completed at least one year of continuous service with Maitland Corporation. The fund was previously limited to staff in supervisory positions. It now provides partial reimbursement for fees paid toward approved courses offered by outside organizations.
How to Apply
Before enrolling in any outside course, employees must submit a Fund Request Form to the Employee Development Office and receive written confirmation of approval. Applications are typically reviewed within five business days. Courses taken without prior authorization are not eligible for reimbursement under any circumstances. Once an approved course has been completed, the employee should file a reimbursement claim along with the original fee receipt and a certificate of completion or passing grade. Claims must be submitted within 60 days of course completion. Approved reimbursements are paid through the employee's regular paycheck within 30 business days of claim submission.
Rate Schedule
Courses are reimbursed at different rates depending on their category, and each category has its own annual ceiling, as shown in the schedule below.
Course Category | Reimbursement Rate | Annual Ceiling |
Job-Related Certification | 80% | $3,000 |
General Professional Skills | 60% | $1,500 |
Personal Enrichment | 40% | $1,500 |
Note: The annual ceiling for each category applies to the combined total of all courses claimed in that category within a single calendar year. Any amount exceeding the ceiling is the responsibility of the employee.
For the Fund Request Form or any questions about the program, contact the Employee Development Office at Ext. 4720.

Please note that no one may begin working under the new method until he or she has attended the briefing session listed for their area. If your regular shift does not overlap with the briefing time shown for your area, please let me know. I will arrange an alternative session so that you can attend at a more convenient time.

Rooftop Terrace — Private Event Use
The rooftop terrace is available for private events hosted by Ridgeway Tower occupant companies with a current lease, provided that a request is submitted at least ten business days in advance. The building's fire safety certificate limits terrace occupancy to 60 persons, so requests exceeding this limit cannot be approved.
Every request must state:
• Event date, start time, and end time
• Expected number of attendees
• Name of the on-site event coordinator from the requesting company
• Whether outside catering or an external vendor will be present
After a request is submitted, it is reviewed by the amenity coordinator within two business days. Written confirmation is sent by e-mail once the request is approved.

Business Briefs
The Bexley District Business Council has opened applications for its annual Community Improvement Grants. The program provides funding to local organizations for neighborhood projects within the district.
The grants are financed through a portion of annual membership fees paid by the Council's 150 member businesses. Eligible applicants must be registered nonprofit groups and must demonstrate that at least 30 percent of total project value will come from volunteer labor or donated materials. Awards fall into three categories: Public Space Enhancement (up to $4,000), Youth and Education Programs (up to $3,500), and Community Safety Improvements (up to $5,000).
"The strongest proposals bring residents together around a shared goal," said Philip Renwick, chair of the grants committee.
Applications are available at bexleycouncil.example and must be submitted by March 15. Decisions will be announced by April 30.
— Bexley Herald
